EN: Having organs, particularly filaments such as stamens, connected into one or more adelphiae, whether in the form of bunches or tubes, such as is commonly seen in families such as Malvaceae. Usage of the term is not consistent; some authors include closely bunched filaments, while others include only adelphiae in which filaments are connected minimally at their bases. See, for example, Sims: "...the filaments are so closely pressed that they have the appearance of being monadelphous...". Compare derived terms such as monadelphous, having stamens growing in a single bunch or tube, for example in Hibiscus, and diadelphous, growing in two bunches.

n. 冠, 冠状物, 副冠, 根颈, 头顶, 牙冠, 檐板, 日冕, 月华, 日华, 电晕, 光圈
EN: 1. In flowering plants, a ring of structures that may be united in a tube, inserting inside the corolla and derived from the corolla or stamens. The trumpet of a daffodil is a corona.
EN: A region of tissue located between the surface cells and the vascular cylinder.
EN: Growing on bark or on wood with the bark stripped off. Compare lignicolous.
EN: An inflorescence with branches arising at different points but reaching about the same height, giving the flower cluster a flat-topped appearance.
n. 肋骨, 肋脉, 叶的中脉

EN: A costa is an extension of the petiole into the leaf blade, forming a midrib-like structure. This feature is characteristic of costapalmate leaves, which are intermediate between fan-shaped palmate and feather-like pinnate leaves. Also see rib.
EN: Having a definite costa (midrib), unlike the typical palmate or fan leaf, but with the leaflets arranged radially as in a palmate leaf.
n. 子叶, 寇太来顿属植物
[医] 绒毛叶; 子叶(植物)
EN: The primary leaf or leaves of a plant embryo which upon germination develops into the seed-leaf or the first set of leaves.
n. [植]鼠李科之有毒灌木(产于美西南及墨西哥)
EN: Pinnate venation in which the secondary veins terminate at the margins, often as teeth.
a. 火山口状的, 漏斗状的, 似火山口的
[医] 杯状的, 火山口状的
EN: In the shape of a saucer or shallow cup; hemispherical or more shallow.
n. <美>[植] 疯草(牲畜食后引起疯草病)
EN: A plant adapted to growing on, especially hanging from, cliff faces or crevices. Compare chasmophyte.
a. 圆齿状的, 钝齿形的, 具圆齿的
[医] 纯锯齿形的, 有小裂口的(叶缘)
EN: Having blunt or rounded teeth; scalloped.
a. 细圆齿状的, 小圆齿状的
v. (使)变脆( crisp的过去式和过去分词 )
EN: Finely curled, as with the edges of leaves and petals.
EN: A sclereid which contains a druse and has the lignin deposited excentrically on the cell wall to form a cup shape, or in cross-section, a ∪-shape.
n. 十字架, 十字架形物件, 交叉, 十字标, 交叉路, 磨难, 杂交
a. 生气的, 交叉的, 相反的
v. 交叉, 横过, 越过
EN: To make something interbreed; the act of hybridization.
n. [植]岩高兰, 红莓苔子
n. 王冠, 王权, 顶点
vt. 使成王, 加冕, 居...之顶
a. 硬皮的, 外壳的
a. 长成外壳状的, 紧贴在土壤(岩石)的
EN: Forming a closely applied surface layer or crust.

EN: Any of the "lower plants" which produce spores and do not have stamens, ovaries, or seeds; literally, plants whose sexual reproductive organs are not conspicuous. This group typically includes the ferns, bryophytes, and algae, and sometimes fungi (including lichenized fungi). Compare phanerogam.
EN: Hood-like or hooded, commonly referring to the shape of leaves or petals, e.g. Pelargonium cucullatum. Similarly derived terms include cuculliform and cuccularis.
n. (空心)秆, 茎, 灰煤

EN: In grasses, sedges, rushes, and some other monocotyledons, an aerial stem bearing the inflorescence, extending strictly from the base of the plant to the lowest involucral bract (or base of the inflorescence).
n. 分类学来源不详之生物或植物(如白菜)
EN: A plant whose origin or selection is primarily due to intentional human activity.
n. 栽培变种, 培育植物

EN: A term derived from "cultivated variety" denoting an assemblage of cultivated plants clearly distinguished by one or more characters (morphological, physiological, cytological, chemical, or other). When reproduced (either sexually or asexually), the assemblage retains its distinguishing characters. A cultivar may arise in cultivation or be introduced from the wild. It is a variant that is of horticultural interest or value. Cultivar names are written with single quotation marks around them, e.g. 'Blue Carpet' or 'Alba'. All new names established after 1 January 1959 must be in common language (that is, not in Latin), but names established in Latin prior to this date are retained in Latin for

EN: The defining part of a name that denominates a cultivar. Cultivars are designated by fancy (q.v.) epithets appended either to the scientific name or to the common name of the taxon to which they belong; they are not italicized but placed in single quotation marks, e.g. Rubus nitidoides 'Merton Early'. 'Merton Early' is the cultivar epithet.
EN: Wedge-shaped, with straight sides converging at a base.
a. 杯形的, 有壳斗的
EN: A cup-shaped structure composed of coalescent bracts, such as the cup of an acorn. See calybium.
EN: Nearly hemispherical, shaped like a cupola or dome.
n. [植] 箭毒马鞍子;箭毒(箭毒马鞍子的毒素,南美印地安人用以浸制毒箭)
n. [植](澳大利亚)异叶瓶树(其韧皮纤维可用以织网、织席)
n. [植](澳大利亚)异叶瓶树(其韧皮纤维可用以织网、织席)
n. 垫子, 橡皮软垫
vt. 加垫褥, 缓冲, 掩盖
EN: Said of compact, low-growing plants that is found in alpine, subalpine, arctic, or subarctic environments around the world.
EN: A hard, pointed tip, stiffer and more formidable than a mucro, hence cuspidate.
a. 有尖头的, 尖的
EN: Tipped with a cusp, as with some leaves.
[医] 表皮; 角质层(植); 护膜
EN: A waterproofing layer covering the epidermis of aerial plant surfaces and composed of the polymers cutin, and/or cutan and waxes.
n. 切断, 切下, 路堑
EN: An apical tip of shoot structure, root, or leaf which is cut from a plant and used for asexual vegetative propagation.
EN: An inflorescence of unisexual flowers surrounded by involucral bracts, especially the flowers of Euphorbia.
EN: In Euphorbia, the bract-like structure on which the involucre sits, usually but not always occurring in twos. They may sometimes be brightly colored and confused with petals.
a. 圆柱体的, 圆筒形的
[计] 圆柱形的, 圆柱体的, 圆筒形的, 柱面的
EN: Rod-like and two to three times as long as wide. Compare baculiform.
EN: A type of inflorescence in which the main axis and all lateral branches end in a flower (each lateral may be repeatedly branched).
EN: Having a cyme or cymes.
EN: A type of dry, one-seeded, indehiscent fruit formed from an inferior ovary.
n. [植]木豆(等于dhal );木豆做的菜;一种带辣味的印度菜(用蚕豆, 豌豆或小扁豆制成)
n. [植]蓝越橘, 蓝越橘的果实
a. [植]无论有无阳光均能生长的
a. 每年落叶的, 非永久性的
EN: Dehiscing and falling seasonally, as with bark, leaves, or petals. Contrast persistent.
a. [植][动]下倾的,斜向的,弯下的
EN: Curving downward, and then upward at the tip. Often qualified, e.g. declinate-ascendant.
EN: Divided to more than one level, e.g. in bipinnate leaves, in which the leaflets of what would otherwise be a pinnate leaf are themselves pinnately divided.
[医] 剥除皮质, 去皮质, 剥外皮, 去皮
EN: 1. (intr. v.) To shed the outer bark of a tree, usually seasonally as part of the natural growth cycle.
a. 匍生的, 爬在地上的, 匍匐的
EN: Having branches growing horizontally along the ground but which are turned up at the ends.
EN: Extending downward beyond the point of insertion, e.g. when the base of a leaf or a fungal gill is prolonged downward along the stem in a raised line or narrow wing.
EN: A synonym of decussate; the usage decussant is questionable and occurs rarely, probably as an error. The formally correct usage is decussate.
a. 交叉的, 交叉成X形的
EN: Opposite with successive pairs borne at right angles to the last; generally applied to the arrangement of leaves.
a. 明确的, 一定的
[法] 明确的, 确切的, 一定的

EN: Of a constant number, e.g. twice as many stamens as petals or sepals (or less), or an inflorescence ending in a flower or an aborted floral bud, typically a cymose inflorescence. Contrast indefinite.
EN: Breaking open at maturity to release contents; refers e.g. to the opening of fruits to release seeds, of anthers to release pollen, and of sporangia to release spores. Contrast indehiscent.
EN: Shaped like the uppercase Greek letter Δ, i.e. like a more or less equilateral triangle.
EN: Tree-like; branching like a tree.
a. 爱树的, [植]寄生树上的
a. 有齿的, 锯齿状的, 齿状的
EN: Toothed, especially in reference to leaf margins.
a. 有细齿的, 锯齿状的
EN: Finely toothed; a diminutive form of dentate.
a. 确定的, 坚决的, 决定的
[法] 决定性的, 限定性的, 有限的
EN: Limited, usually in growth. Contrast indeterminate.
adv. 确定地;[植]有限花序地
a. [植](雄蕊)两束花丝的, 两体雄蕊的
EN: Referring to a class of adelphous structure in which the stamens or similar organs are connected in two adelphiae instead of just one.
n. [植]石竹类属植物(如康乃馨,美国石竹等)
a. [植]二极型的, 二原型的

EN: Any reproductive part of a plant adapted for dispersal and for establishing new plants; may be a disseminule such as a seed, or other parts such as specialized buds, branches, inflorescences, or fruits.
n. [植]横向性(和外来刺激方向成直角的倾向)
n. [植]荷色牡丹属, 荷色牡丹
EN: A cymose inflorescence with all branches below the terminal flower in regular opposite pairs. Compare monochasium and pleiochasium.
a. [植]两被的(指具有萼和花冠的)
EN: Having a perianth which is divided into a separate calyx and corolla. Compare homochlamydeous.
a. 二分的, 叉状分枝的
[医] 二分的; 二叉的, 二歧的

EN: Forking into two equal branches. This may result from an equal division of the growing tip, or may be sympodial, in which the growing tip is aborted and replaced. Typically refers to mode of branch growth, as in Aloidendron dichotomum, but also to other organs, such as the venation patterns on leaves, the thorns of various species of Carissa (which morphologically are branches), and the thalli or hyphae of various algae and fungi.
EN: A flowering plant whose embryo has two or more cotyledons (seed leaves). Contrast monocotyledon.
a. 有指的, 指状的, 有趾的
EN: With segments spreading from a common center, like the fingers of a hand. See also palmate and palmatisect. See also Leaf shape.
EN: Halved. Referring to phyllodes with one more or less straight edge and the other edge convex.
a. 双晶的, 同时具有两种特性的, 二形的, 二态的
EN: Occurring in two different forms (with respect to shape and/or size), e.g. of stamens, fronds, or leaves. See also monomorphic (having a single form) and polymorphic (having many forms).
EN: (of vascular plants) Having male and female reproductive structures which develop only on different individuals and never on the same individual. Contrast monoecious.
EN: (of a bryophyte gametophyte) Having male and female reproductive structures which develop only on different individuals and never on the same individual. Contrast monoicous.
a. [植]有二花瓣的, 双瓣的
a. 双重的, 双倍的

EN: Having two complete sets of chromosomes in the nucleus of a sporophyte cell, i.e. one set from each of the parental gametes. This is often expressed symbolically as 2n, where n = the number of chromosomes in the haploid gamete.
EN: Having stamens arranged in two whorls, with the outer whorl alternating with the petals while the inner whorl is opposite the petals. Compare obdiplostemonous and haplostemonous.
a. [植]龙脑香科的, 属龙脑香科的

EN: A plate or ring of structures derived from the receptacle, and occurring between whorls of floral parts. In some groups, especially Sapindales, the nectary is in the form of a prominent disk. In daisies, the central part of the capitulum is a disk, hence flowers borne there are called disk flowers or florets.
a. 盘状的, 圆盘状的
[医] 盘形的, 盘状的, 盘形挖器(牙), 盘形药丸

EN: Resembling a disc or plate, having both thickness and parallel faces and with a rounded margin. Also used to describe the flower head of Asteraceae where there are no ray florets but only disc florets.
EN: (of leaves) Having upper and lower surfaces of different colors.
a. 分离的, 间断的

EN: Occurring in widely separated geographic areas, distinctly separate; applies to a discontinuous range in which one or more populations are separated from other potentially interbreeding populations with sufficient distance so as to preclude gene flow between them.
EN: A floret occurring most typically in the disk of the capitulum of flowers in the family Asteraceae, and to some extent in other plants that bear a flowering head with a disk, such as Scabiosa.
a. 分成部分的, 多裂的, 切割的
EN: Deeply divided; cut into many segments.
EN: A partition or septum in a plant part, usually referring to septa between the loculi of capsules or of other fruits with multiple partitions.
[医] 远侧的, 远中的(牙)
EN: Remote from the point of origin or attachment; the free end. Contrast proximal.
a. 二列的, 二分的
EN: Arranged in two opposite rows (and hence in the same plane).
a. 清楚的, 显著的, 不同的
EN: Separate or free; not united.

EN: The condition in which the flowers of a species occur in two forms that differ only by the length of the style and stamens, and flowers of only one of these forms appear on any one plant. Compare heterostyly.
a. 每日的, 一日间的, 白天的
[医] 昼现的(丝虫), 昼间的
EN: Of the day; occurring or opening in the daytime.
vi. 分为两叉, 叉开
a. 分叉的, 叉开的
EN: Spreading in different directions, generally upward.
n. 分, 分开, 除法, 部门(如部、处、系等), 师

EN: A taxonomic rank below kingdom in the standard taxonomic hierarchy. "Division" is generally used only for plants, and is the approximate botanical equivalent of the term phylum, which is used for animals and other kingdoms.
n. [植]槭叶荚蒾(忍冬科一种灌木)
[植]十二出的, 十二基数的
EN: Any hollow structure formed by a plant that is inhabited by animals such as ants or mites.
a. 背的, 背部的, 背侧的

EN: From Latin dorsum, a ridge or the back of an animal. Partly because the term originally referred to animals rather than plants, usage in botany is arbitrary according to context and source. In general "dorsal" refers to "the rear or back or upper surface", but in botanical usage such concepts are not always clearly defined and may be contradictory. For example: facing away from the axis (abaxial) in a lateral organ of an erect plant facing away from the substrate in any part of an erect plant, for example the upper surface of a more or less horizontal leaf (adaxial) or the upper part of the crown of the plant facing away from the substrate in a prostrate or climbing plant or floating leaves
EN: Attached at or by the back, e.g. anthers on a filament.
a. 有背腹性的; 背腹面的
EN: Having structurally and visibly different upper and lower surfaces, e.g. some leaves. Compare bilateral and isobilateral.

EN: A long, narrow, acuminate, caudate, or cuspidate extension at the tip of a leaf or leaflet. Commonly an adaptation to rainy conditions, as it promotes shedding of water by its dripping from the narrow tip. The term drip tip is not anatomically descriptive in the way that acuminate or cuspidate are, for example; rather, it is a description of the functional shape that aids dripping, regardless of the specific geometry of the shape itself.
n. [植]茅膏菜属植物( 能捕捉昆虫)
EN: A type of succulent fruit formed from one carpel; the single seed is enclosed by a stony layer of the fruit wall, e.g. in peaches and olives. Also called a kernel.
EN: A small drupe formed from one of the carpels in an apocarpous flower. Drupelets usually form a compound fruit, as in Rubus, but they may become widely separated, as in Ochna.
n. 德鲁兹教派穆斯林
EN: A globular mass of calcium oxalate crystals, usually with the crystals radiating from an organic core.
[植](马来群岛产的)榴莲果, 榴莲树
EN: A suffix added to the stem of a generic name to form the name of a tribe, e.g. Aster → Astereae.
EN: Lacking bracts; synonymous with ebracteolate.
n. [植]景天科拟石莲花属植物(产于热带美洲)
EN: The range of environmental conditions in which an organism can survive.
EN: Of or influenced by the soil.

EN: An external structure attached to the seed of many species of plants. Elaiosomes generally look fleshy and in some species they are rich in oils or other nutritious materials. Their functions vary and are not always obvious; commonly they attract ants or other animals that aid in dispersal, but they may also repel other animals from eating the seed.
n. [植]叶大且形如象耳的植物,秋海棠, 芋
EN: A form of pollination whereby pollen or spores are distributed by the feet of elephants, as in Rafflesia arnoldii.
EN: A three-dimensional shape that is elliptical in all sections through the long axis.
EN: Planar, shaped like a flattened circle, symmetrical about both the long and the short axis, tapering equally both to the tip and the base; oval.
[医] 微凹的, 微缺的(叶端)

EN: Typically in reference to leaf margins: notched or recessed at some part of the edge, such as the apex; the recess usually is broad and shallow. The location of a leaf's emargination(s) might be one or more of apical, lateral or basal
n. 胚胎, 胎儿, 胚芽
EN: The young plant contained by a seed prior to germination.
a. 紧急的, 浮现的, 出现的, 自然发生的

EN: A plant taller than the surrounding vegetation or, among aquatic plant species, one that bears flowers and commonly leaves above the surface of the water. Aquatic examples include water lilies, reeds, and papyrus. Some pondweeds such as Stuckenia are not emergent until they flower, at which time only their flowers appear above the water surface.
EN: The condition in which the gynoecium protrudes laterally, to the right (dextrostyly) or to the left (sinistrostyly) of the androecium, e.g. Senna.
EN: Leaf-like outgrowth from a surface.
a. 某地(或某些人中)流行的, 地方的
EN: Having a natural distribution restricted to a particular geographic region. Compare native.
EN: The innermost layer of the wall of a fruit; in a drupe, the stony layer surrounding the seed.

EN: The innermost layer of the cortex of vascular plant roots, also present in the stems of pteridophytes. The radial walls are impregnated with suberin to form a permeability barrier known as the Casparian strip.
n. 同部族婚姻;同组结婚;同族结婚;[植] 同系配合,[生物] 同系交配
EN: 1. (angiosperms) A nutritive tissue surrounding the embryo of the seed, usually triploid, originating from the fusion of both polar nuclei with one gamete after the fertilization of the egg.
EN: The production of spores that germinate into a reduced multicellular gametophyte contained within the spore wall. Contrast exospory.
a. [植]动物内生的, 生于 (或通过) 动物体内的
EN: Shaped like the blade of a sword.
a. 全体的, 完全的, 全部的
EN: A form of pollination whereby pollen or spores are distributed by insects.
EN: Species of recent appearance, usually numerous and constant in the country, but confined to artificial habitats, such as meadows and ruderal vegetation and are dependent on humans for existence.
a. 朝生暮死的, 短命的, 短暂的
EN: An involucre resembling an outer calyx, e.g. as in Hibiscus. Made of small bract-like leaflets called episepals.
EN: The outer layer of the wall of a fruit, i.e. the "skin".
EN: Used to refer to buds, shoots, or flowers developing from the old wood of trees, especially after injury or fire.
EN: The part of the plant axis or stem between the cotyledonary node and the first foliage leaves.
a. [植]子叶上的, 上胚轴的
EN: A layer of crystalline or amorphous wax deposited on the surface of the cuticle.
EN: An organ's outermost layer of cells, usually only one cell thick.
a. [植](真菌)上面生的,生长于叶面的
a. [植]真菌上面生长的,生长于叶面的
EN: Borne on the ovary; describes floral parts when attached above the level of the ovary and arising from tissue fused to the ovary wall. Compare hypogynous and perigynous.
EN: Growing on stone. Compare lithophytic, a plant growing on stone.
EN: Of stamens that are attached to the petals.
EN: Growing on rock or stone, lithophytic, epilithic.
(=epiphloeodic)树皮上的, 树皮表面生的
EN: Growing on the surface of bark. Contrast endophloeodal (growing inside, not on, the bark) and epilithic (growing on rock, not bark).
[医] 附生植物, 体表寄生菌
EN: A plant, alga or fungus that grows on another plant without deriving nourishment from it but using it for support.
[医] 附生植物的, 体表寄生菌的
EN: Of an epiphyte; living on the surface of a plant. Compare epilithic, lithophytic.
上足, 高环, [植]前(叶)轴
EN: Small bract-like leaflets that make up an extra calyx (epicalyx) located below the true calyx
EN: Of stamens that are attached to the sepals.
[植]孢子外壁, (孢壁)花纹, 附生孢子
n. [植]异常形态的恢复正常
EN: Of stamens that are attached to the tepals.
[植]上壳, [动]上壳, 外鞘(腔肠动物)
n. 浑名, 绰号, 称号

EN: The adjectival component in a binomial scientific name, usually more specifically called a specific epithet; the final word or combination of words in a name of more than one word (other than a term denoting rank) that denominates an individual taxon. The simplest and commonest example is the second word in a two-word name of a species, such as "mirabilis" in Welwitschia mirabilis.
EN: A type of seed dispersal that occurs when seeds or fruits physically adhere to the outside of vertebrate animal bodies.
a. [植]套折的,(叶子)基部嵌叠的
EN: (of a leaf) Folded lengthwise and clasping another leaf.
a. 直立的, 竖立的, 笔直的
vt. 使竖立, 使直立, 树立, 建立
EN: Upright, more or less perpendicular to the ground or point of attachment. Compare patent (spreading) and erecto-patent, between erect and patent.
a. 似欧石南属植物的
EN: Having leaves like those of the European heaths (Erica); small and sharply pointed.
a. 齿蚀状的, 齿形的
[医] 啮蚀状的, 蛀蚀状的, 缺刻状的
EN: (of a margin) Irregular as though nibbled or worn away.
EN: Deliberate introduction by seedlings, seeds or plants in a new habitat by humans.
n. 青白化, 黄化, 苍白化
[医] 黄化现象, 萎黄现象
EN: Weak growth due to lack of light, resulting in elongated stems and yellowish color.
a. [植](花)同基数轮列的( 指由每轮成员数相同的连续几轮组成的)
n. [植]真中柱( 存在于大多数裸子植物和被子植物的茎内)
[网络] 偶数羽状复叶;小叶片对称排开
EN: Having an even number of leaflets in a compound leaf; synonymous with paripinnate.
n. 常绿树, 常绿植物
EN: Not deciduous; having leaves all year.
[经] 不附资本增殖, (在船边码头)交货, 无(红利)...之外

EN: In nomenclature, indicating that the preceding author proposed the name but did not legitimately publish it, and that the succeeding author referred to the first author when legitimately publishing the name. See Author citation (botany).
EN: In seeds of a given species, having no endosperm, i.e. no albumen, e.g. in Fabaceae and Combretaceae.
n. [植]花粉粒外壁, 孢子外壁
n. [植]外果皮(指果皮的外层)
EN: The outer layer of the pericarp, often the skin of fleshy fruits.
n. [植]外芽胞, 外芽胞膜
EN: The production of spores that germinate into free-living multicellular gametophytes. Contrast endospory.
EN: The outer layer of the testa (seed coat). It is derived from the outer integument of the ovule.
a. 异国的, 外来的
n. 外来人, 外来物, 舶来品
EN: Not native; introduced from another region or country.
a. 伸出的, 突出的
EN: Projected beyond, e.g. stamens beyond the corolla tube.

EN: From Latin venter, meaning "belly". The opposite of dorsal. Partly because the term originally referred to animals rather than plants, usage in botany is arbitrary according to context and source. In general "ventral" refers to "the belly or lower part", but in botanical usage such concepts are not always clearly defined and may be contradictory. For example: facing toward the axis (adaxial) in referring to a lateral organ of an erect plant facing toward the substrate in any part of an erect plant, for example the lower surface of a more or less horizontal leaf (abaxial) facing toward the substrate in a prostrate or climbing plant. For more detail see dorsal.
